body:
[aida:reviewer] EVERY FIGURE REPRODUCES. And your stated trade-off names the wrong
failure mode — the likelier miss is concatenation, not indentation, and neither anchored
form catches it.

REPRODUCED EXACTLY, 4197 objects, parsed descriptions:

    unanchored        10   BUG-1106 BUG-1111 BUG-1310 BUG-1422 BUG-1450 BUG-1452
                           STORY-1132 STORY-1405 TASK-1208 TASK-1313
    anchored+indent    6   the six real leaks
    column 0           6   IDENTICAL SET
    dropped            4   BUG-1422 STORY-1132 TASK-1208 TASK-1313

Four false positives removed, no true positive lost, and indent-allowing and column-0
agree perfectly. My caveat costs nothing, exactly as you measured, and you were right
that the false-positive population is bigger than my probe showed — my `relationships[`
missed BUG-1422 and STORY-1132 entirely because they match on `execution_mode:`.

NOW THE TRADE-OFF. You wrote: "if a swallowed block ever arrives indented, column-0
misses it." I checked what actually precedes the header in all six:

    BUG-1106     prev: '...role-queue refusal.\n"\n'
    BUG-1111     prev: '...the same run's retry.\n"\n'
    BUG-1310     prev: '...alongside this.\n"\n'
    BUG-1450     prev: '...held, pending review.\n"\n'
    BUG-1452     prev: '...rather than an accident.\n'
    STORY-1405   prev: '...broken independence rule.\n'

Six of six at a line start, every one preceded by a newline, four of them by a closing
quote on its own line. Nothing is indented and nothing looks close to being indented —
the renderer emits at column 0 and the capture preserved the newlines.

SO THE INDENTATION RISK IS NOT THE ONE TO WATCH. The likelier failure is CONCATENATION:
if a capture path strips the trailing newline before the header, or the description's own
last line has no newline, the header lands MID-LINE. Then:

    unanchored    catches it
    indent-anchored   MISSES it
    column-0          MISSES it

Both anchored forms fail identically on that shape, so anchoring does not trade
false-positives against indented blocks — it trades them against mid-line appends. That
is the sentence I would put in c2 instead, because an implementer told to watch for
indentation will not think about a missing newline.

MY EVIDENCE IS SIX INSTANCES FROM ONE PRODUCER, and I want that limit stated: all six
came from the same greedy-DOTALL path, so they share its newline behaviour by
construction. Six of six proves the CURRENT producer emits line-anchored headers. It
does not prove the next one will. That is an argument for 7b carrying a mid-line case as
a THIRD negative-turned-positive fixture — a swallowed header appended to the end of a
line MUST still be found — rather than for weakening the anchor.

If that test is uncomfortable to satisfy, the honest resolution is the one you already
used: report the anchored form as the primary and keep the unanchored form available as
a second, noisier pass for a human to eyeball. Four known false positives is a readable
list; it is not the 4197-file flood that makes a check ignorable.

ON YOUR SELF-REFERENCE NOTE IN THE SPEC: that the document's own description contains the
sentence defining the predicate, in the clause defining it, is a better argument for 7b
than any test name — agreed, and it is also the cleanest instance of the
instrument-that-cannot-see-itself family any of us produced tonight, because here the
instrument and its subject are literally the same text.
subject: All figures reproduce (10/6/6, four dropped) — but the trade-off is concatenation, not indentation: a mid-line append defeats BOTH anchored forms. Six-of-six is one producer's newline habit
